issue_context.title: WebApplicationFactory.Client should fail with DisposedException but does not.
issue_context.body:
@javiercn thanks, but I did know this and had already fixed this in the real code before raising this issue. It’s why I wrote this in the first message:

> How can I test that properly? The purpose of this test is to pretty much test the whole thing (of course excluding some mocks (not shown) that we have set up and tested elsewhere).
> 
> Of course I just fixed the mistake, but I would have liked to see this fail before finding out somewhere else.

The problem I have is that the test succeeds and didn’t find this error.

_Originally posted by @Rubenisme in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33601#issuecomment-863415398_

This is just the continuation of the previous since it was closed by the bot and not resolved.
comments:
So the HttpRequestMessage and the HttpContent are disposed mid call but that doesn't cause an exception in the test server? For reference, what kind of HttpContent is it?

First, this looks like a race condition. The using block that disposes the request/content doesn't exit until the http operation becomes async. A normal http client might have to resolve dns, open a connection, serialize the headers, etc., lots of async work before sending the request. The in-memory one bypasses all of that overhead and can start reading the content almost immediately. I think this is happening before we even start reading the headers:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a9a6831a1a0aa2fc21c276e1f28b86a2b1cdbb28/src/Hosting/TestHost/src/ClientHandler.cs#L71-L97

The in-memory flow does force server side processing off onto another thread, but not until later:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a9a6831a1a0aa2fc21c276e1f28b86a2b1cdbb28/src/Hosting/TestHost/src/HttpContextBuilder.cs#L94-L99

A fix for this would require delaying the call to the SendRequestStream callback until after the thread hop in HttpContextBuilder.SendAsync. Arguably that's when it should happen anyways since it's weird to read the request body before 'sending' the headers.

cc: @JamesNK who last refactored that code path.

Thanks so much @javiercn and @Tratcher, that makes sense that it happens so quickly in the test. I actually tried to add some middleware in the test later to delay the connection to see if that might be the cause but couldn’t get that working as hoped. Still had somehow excepted some check of disposal. Thanks for looking into this, this is one of those things that you’d like the test to reveal.

We've moved this issue to the Backlog milestone. This means that it is not going to be worked on for the coming release. We will reassess the backlog following the current release and consider this item at that time. To learn more about our issue management process and to have better expectation regarding different types of issues you can read our [Triage Process](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).
@Rubenisme If @Tratcher is ok with it and you want to try and send us a PR I think we would accept one. I'm ok with it at the very least, however @Tratcher is the expert here, so I delegate to him.
It should be possible to store and delay the SendRequestStream callback until RunRequestAsync, I just don't know what affect it will have on existing tests. Feel free to try it.
Would it be ok if I worked on this issue?

Yes, that’d be great. I tried to look at it and had it reproduced in a unit test in the hosting tests project but didn’t see an immediate solution. I haven’t given it more priority since, but have thought about it recently again, glad you are having some time for this.

review_comments:
Is there a race here? Could the SendAsync call finish before the message is disposed?

Is the best way to force the error to dispose the StringContent before calling SendAsync?

Yes, that seemed to be happend in CI. I have adjusted the test to manually dispose the `HttpContent` but that means that it will throw in `Configure` instead of `SendRequestStream`.
I also added another test which always throws in `SendRequestStream`.
